Synapse. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of inference. Information is your home. Other people travel through it. You live there.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).
  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around MND (Mind)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.
  • Predictive Cache. 1/Soma Break, when an enemy you can see takes an action, you may have anticipated it: reroll the lowest die on the next reaction or attack you make against that enemy this round.

“Reality is a database. You brought admin tools.”

Yesod-Diver. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret metaphysical constructs (Sparks, slippage, noospheric entities). 1/Soma Break, you can ask the GM one direct question about a nearby “system,” and receive a truthful but incomplete answer.

"Strike the clause. Insert your own. Reality reads from the top."

The Cosmic Linguist edits reality like text — meaning first, matter second. One currency now: Surge. The editor always has the next word, so you bank +1 Surge at the start of your turn (the old Resonance, Strain, and Editorial Authority pools are folded into this single pool).

The Edit (spent via Surge)

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast resists counter / dispel (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves are at disadvantage (only one correct interpretation: yours).
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves at disadvantage; allies near you bank a reroll.

The Sentence endures as your signature stance — while held, the manifestation's primary target is bound by name and rolls its checks against you at disadvantage.

description.value:
"Magic is grammar. Reality is a draft."

You are a prepared, academic manifestant who edits meaning directly. You do not delegate power; you channel it raw.

Engine truth: your craft runs on Clarity (your casting pool, deeper than other paths), Noise (the lattice hears sloppy work), Surge (the editor's one currency — +1 at the start of your turn), and Blood Debt (reaching above your tier, discounted by your Discipline). The cast dialog's cost line is the truth.

An earlier draft of this class spoke of Resonance, Strain, and correspondence alignment. Those pools were folded into Surge — the fiction survives; the bookkeeping does not.

The Edit — Surge spends, allocated in the cast dialog.

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast resists counter/dispel (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves are at disadvantage: in the dialog this raises your working's save DC and forces the target to roll 3d10 keep-lowest-2. Only one correct interpretation: yours.
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves at disadvantage; allies near you bank a reroll.

These are the old Resonance channels spoken in the one currency: Surge. The Sentence (Initiation 11) endures as your signature stance on top of them.

"I am not casting. I am editing."

Roleplay register, not rules. Choose the voice of your edits — Additive, Subtractive, Transformative, Referential, or Performative. Narrate every manifestation in your mode: it shapes how the working looks, sounds, and is remembered — never what it costs.

The cast dialog's cost line is the truth. (An earlier draft priced modes in Strain; Strain is retired.)

Doctrine: Prefer surgical changes with precise scope — a small note that produces a large consequence. You are strongest when the edit looks modest.

The Annotator wins in the margins. Your Surge spends are footnotes with teeth: shore up an ally's roll, pin a foe with marginalia it cannot ignore, and revise the whole passage at once.

Doctrine (spent via Surge)

  • Footnote (1) — an ally banks a reroll-lowest (a small note, a large consequence).
  • Marginalia (2) — a foe is Staggered and rolls its saves at disadvantage.
  • Revision (5) — allies within 6 squares each bank a reroll-lowest (the whole passage, corrected).

“You already know. You just refuse to say it too early.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The High Priestess (Seer). You read the invisible pressure in a room before anyone else admits it exists. You are intuition weaponized, omen-bearing, and very difficult to surprise in ways that matter.

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Abyssal Cartographers.

“There are maps beneath the map.”

Abyssal Cartographers chart what most people refuse to admit exists: drowned tunnels, pressure-cut caverns, forgotten ferry lines, and the strange geometry of places where water remembers older routes than roads do. They do not merely travel hidden ways. They prove those ways were always there.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Investigation.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Understanding - Structure gives shape to power. +1 Intrigue, +1 Logistics OPs

Binah is discernment, containment, and the discipline to make dangerous ideas survivable. It rewards planning, governance, and strategic control that turns chaos into infrastructure.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Kabbalist.

“The map is not the territory. The territory is also not the territory.”

Kabbalists are not wizards. They are cartographers of meaning — the kind who draw a line and the world decides it has always been there.

They study the Tree the way an engineer studies a bridge: load, strain, failure points, and where the pressure is going when nobody is looking. Sephiroth is flow. Qliphoth is leak. And if you learn the geometry well enough, you can reroute the flood before it drowns the region.

To a Kabbalist, the Great Work is not aspiration. It is alignment. Name the thing correctly, place it correctly, and reality stops wasting energy pretending to be something else.

How Kabbalists pursue the Great Work:

  • By reading Hexes like paragraphs — sephirothic intent, qliphothic rot, and the lies in-between
  • By reducing the cost of identifying Sparks and metaphysical conditions
  • By treating the Tree as infrastructure rather than metaphor
  • By shifting alignment deliberately, even when the world pushes back

Resonance: Tree / Binah-Tiferet axis — structure, pattern-recognition, and the disciplined naming of what is actually happening.

Tell-tales: finger-traced grids, muttered node-names, diagrams drawn over maps that somehow make the maps more true.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Soft Power OP rolls

Cost Principle: Kabbalistic order clarifies, but clarification creates strain. When you force alignment, hidden contradictions surface somewhere else.

item.lore:
A cheap, mass-produced stiletto with an apology engraved up the fuller. The engraving is competent. The steel is mediocre. The point is sharp. They were sold in bulk before the Shattering as novelty items at gas stations. After the Shattering, somebody noticed they actually work — and not just in the obvious ways.

Mercy Engraving. When you reduce a creature to 0 Integrity with this knife, the kill incurs no Blood Debt. The engraved apology counts. Reality accepts the receipt. (Mal: "Don't think about this too hard. The metaphysics are at minimum dubious. The mechanic is real.")

manifestation.concept: When something in the world errs — a swing goes wide, a lie lands badly, a claim fails — Marginalia appends the editorial mark [sic] beside it. Thus it was written. The error is not corrected; it is preserved, deliberately, as part of the target's text, where everyone can read it. The cruelest thing an Annotator can do is not fix your mistake — it's make your mistake canonical.
manifestation.durationText: The mark holds one round — long enough to be cited.
manifestation.triggerText: When a creature she can see fails a roll or misses — the error must be witnessed, fresh, and genuine.
manifestation.targetText: One creature whose failure she witnessed
manifestation.rangeAreaText: Sight — if she can read the error, she can cite it.
manifestation.riskText: A [sic] is a claim of accuracy. If the Annotator mis-cites — marks as error something that was true — the mark reverts to her own text: she takes the Resolve penalty herself, and the record remembers who wrote it.
manifestation.pathResonance: Annotator doctrine under a Binah anchor: the world is a text, and a text is improved by honest marginalia. She does not punish error — she preserves it, so the record can learn. The answer is in the text. It is always in the text.
manifestation.signature: The mark is always in red, always in her hand, and always spelled correctly — even in languages she has never studied, [sic] renders in Marginalia's handwriting.
manifestation.thirdThing: The mark appears a fraction of a second before the error finishes happening — as if the record already knew.

members.name: Voss Ammering
members.notes: Marginalia pulled her out of a flooded chart-vault with three ribs cracked and the only surviving copy of the Undersill Rutter clutched to her chest; she still won't say what she saw down there, and she's never asked Marginalia to explain why they went back for the map before her.

members.name: Petra Coyle-Ness
members.notes: Keeps a ledger of every depth Marginalia ever lied about in a survey report, not out of spite but because someone in the Errata Society has to remember the truth, and she's decided that someone is her.

members.name: Bram Utterlyne
members.notes: Owes Marginalia a debt neither of them names anymore: he held the light steady for six hours in the Choked Fathom while Marginalia redrew a passage from memory, and he's fairly sure that's the only reason either of them came up breathing.

members.name: Corvin Ashtabel
members.notes: He carved the correction into a load-bearing glyph that saved Marginalia's arm at Threshhold Nine, and the stiffness never left his own hands — he still sends the bill as a joke, but he means it a little.

members.name: Prudence Okwuosa
members.notes: Marginalia talked her down from over-tuning the Tiferet node when the feedback started rewriting her sense of time; she remembers the sound of that voice more clearly than her own name that week.

members.name: Denny Halsic
members.notes: Owes Marginalia a bottle of the good ink and a proper apology, in that order, for the ledger error that nearly collapsed a path they were both standing on.
